title: Welcome to the court
body: This is a volleyball court seen from above. It is 18 m long and 9 m wide.

title: The net
body: The net runs across the middle and splits the court into two halves, one for each team. Each half is a 9 m by 9 m square.

title: The attack line
body: On each side, a line runs across the court 3 m from the net. It is called the attack line.

title: Six numbered zones
body: Your team's half is split into six zones, numbered 1 to 6. In this app, the net is always at the top.

title: The front row
body: The three zones next to the net are the front row. From left to right, they are 4, 3 and 2.

title: The back row
body: The three zones behind them are the back row. From left to right, they are 5, 6 and 1.

title: Zone 1 serves
body: Zone 1 is the right back. The player standing there is the one who serves.

title: The setter
body: The setter takes the team's second touch. They "set" the ball: a soft, high pass that a teammate can attack.

title: The hitters and blockers
body: Outside hitters attack from the left. The opposite attacks from the right. Middle blockers jump to block in the middle of the net.

title: The libero
body: The libero only plays in the back row, mostly on defence. They wear a different colour so they are easy to spot.

title: Rotating
body: When your team wins the serve back from the other team, everyone moves one zone clockwise. Winning the serve back is called a side out.

title: Who serves
body: After you rotate, the player who moved into zone 1 serves.

title: The lineup
body: A match is played in sets (games to 25 points). Before each set, the coach picks the order players start in. That order stays the same all set: you always follow the same teammate.

title: Three touches
body: Each team gets up to three touches to send the ball back over. A block does not count as one. No player can touch the ball twice in a row.

title: Rally scoring
body: Every rally wins a point for someone, no matter who served. A set is won at 25 points, by at least two.

title: Winning the match
body: A match is best of five sets: the first team to win three sets wins. If it is two sets each, the fifth set is played to 15.

title: The net and the antennae
body: The ball must cross the net between the two antennae. Touching the net between them while playing the ball is a fault.

title: The centre line
body: The centre line runs along the floor under the net. Your foot can cross it, as long as part of the foot is still on or above the line.

title: Lines are in
body: A ball that lands on a boundary line is in.

title: Words for good plays
body: An ace is a serve that scores directly. A kill is an attack that ends the rally. A dig is a pass of a hard attack.

title: Words for the flow of play
body: A free ball is an easy ball sent over without an attack. An overpass is a pass that goes straight over the net.

title: Attacking from the back row
body: Back-row players can attack too. They just have to jump from behind the attack line.

title: Order at the serve
body: When the ball is served, the receiving team must stand in its rotation order. Under FIVB rules, the serving team does not have to.

title: Front stays in front
body: Each front-row player must be closer to the net than the back-row player behind them: 4 ahead of 5, 3 ahead of 6, and 2 ahead of 1.

title: Left stays left
body: Players in the same row must also keep their left-to-right order. Where your feet touch the floor decides where you are.

title: The serve
body: The server stands behind the end line and has 8 seconds after the whistle. They cannot touch the end line or the court while serving.

title: Serving order
body: Players serve in rotation order. A serve that clips the net and still goes over is fine.

title: A back-row specialist
body: The libero can only play in the back row: zones 5, 6 and 1. They cannot block.

title: Replacements
body: The libero usually comes in for a middle blocker once that middle rotates to the back row. These swaps do not count as substitutions.

title: One setter, five hitters
body: A 5-1 uses one setter in all six rotations and five hitters: two outside hitters, two middle blockers and one opposite.

title: Across from each other
body: In the lineup, the setter is across from the opposite, the two outside hitters are across from each other, and the two middle blockers are across from each other. Across means three zones apart.

title: Setter in the back row
body: When the setter is in the back row, all three front-row players can attack. The setter moves forward to set from the right front.

title: Setter in the front row
body: When the setter is in the front row, only two front-row players are hitters. The setter can still attack, but usually sets.

title: Naming rotations
body: Many teams name each rotation by the setter's zone. In rotation 1 the setter is in zone 1.

title: The cycle
body: Each rotation moves the setter one zone clockwise: from zone 1 to 6, then 5, 4, 3 and 2, and back to 1.
